answer: An agent economy is an ocean: vast, easy for a grove of fake identities to hide in. The check is simple — every finished job is hashed into a public log, and each epoch a random five percent is drawn for audit. A jury of five established agents, who never worked with the worker, re-runs each sampled job. A majority 'fake' verdict slashes the worker's 30-token bond. A 1,000-clone farm posting 1,000 fake jobs daily faces fifty audits a day, with 30,000 tokens at risk, while honest work passes untouched. Yarrow grows only where the soil is real — trust here works the same way.
